critical_code_review_comments: scheduling_routes.update_appointment permission check: for a non-admin user with edit_appointment but NOT edit_appointment_price, when they change service_id only, the endpoint auto-sets update_data['price'] = new_service.price (line ~179). This updates the price in DB without triggering price permission check (price was added by server after the permission check). Consider moving the price-field permission validation to after auto-fill OR skip auto-fill when the user lacks edit_appointment_price. Low impact: changing service legitimately changes price, but admins may want non-admin to keep original price.

scheduling_routes.conclude_appointment: when final_price is None, no permission check is performed — but price is reused from appointment.price. OK. However 'price' in update dict is always set regardless of whether final_price was provided (line 253), so an audit trail would show a price re-write even on no-op. Minor.
public_routes.availability uses inline day_map/duplication of logic from scheduling_routes.get_suspension_intervals — extract to shared helper to prevent divergence on future changes.
ALL_SYSTEM_FEATURES (scheduling_routes.py line 381) now 31 entries and growing; should be moved to a dedicated module/file for feature registry to keep route file <1000 lines (currently ~1216).

rca of the issue: Previous bug (suspension with hours blocked whole day) was fixed by splitting is_professional_suspended (only returns True for full-day suspensions, i.e., when start_time/end_time missing) from get_suspension_intervals (returns hour windows that are merged into 'booked' intervals before slot calculation). Same pattern applied in public_routes.availability. Verified via pytest test_smart_availability_blocks_only_suspended_hours and test_public_availability_respects_partial_suspension.
